items.title: 13.3.1 Types of Animals on the basis of Heat Source

items: Ectotherms gain most of their body heat from outside; their temperature tends to follow the surroundings. Most invertebrates, and fishes, amphibians and reptiles, are ectotherms. Their metabolic rate is too low to keep them warm, so they use behaviour: basking in the sun (radiation) or lying on warm rock (conduction) when cold, and seeking shade or burrowing when hot; in very cold climates they become dormant.

Endotherms generate most of their body heat by internal metabolism and keep a fairly constant temperature, often above that of the surroundings. Birds and mammals are endotherms; in the cold they shiver or burn brown adipose tissue, and most have insulation such as hair, feathers or fat.
